answerNotes.CRACKER: Table crackers are associated especially with British Christmas traditions and are also enjoyed elsewhere.
answerNotes.CROWN: The folded paper crown is a party hat, not a valuable headpiece.

answerNotes.TUBE: The tube gives the paper favor its central shape.
answerNotes.SNAP: Snap names the sound-making strip as well as its brief noise.

answerNotes.NATIVITY: Nativity displays vary; not every arrangement contains the same figures.

answerNotes.JOSEPH: Joseph is commonly included in household Nativity displays.
answerNotes.SHEPHERD: Shepherd figures are associated with the account in Luke's Gospel.

description: Explore a traditional German Christmas decoration through its tiers, figures, and warm-air-driven rotor.
cardDescription: Explore a traditional German Christmas decoration through its tiers, figures, and warm-air-driven rotor.
focus: A candle-powered Christmas pyramid turns when rising warm air moves the blades above its displayed figures.

answerNotes.PYRAMID: A Christmas pyramid is a decorative rotating structure, not an ancient stone monument.
answerNotes.ROTOR: The rotor captures moving air and transfers motion to the display.
answerNotes.CANDLE: Some modern versions use different power sources instead of candle heat.
answerNotes.TIER: Tiers organize the scene into stacked display levels.
answerNotes.AXLE: The axle connects rotating parts rather than providing the heat source.

answerNotes.FELT: Felt does not need the same woven edge finishing as many cloth fabrics.

answerNotes.APPLIQUE: Applique adds a surface design, unlike cutting a hole through the cloth.
answerNotes.SLIT: The opening lets the covering be placed around an already standing tree.
